newsitem.title: USA: HOT STOCKS HIGHLIGHTS - Mergers & Acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: HOT STOCKS HIGHLIGHTS - Mergers & Acquisitions.

text.p: It was another Merger Monday for Wall Street with a battery of deals and merger plan updates announced, including:

MCI Communications Corp and British Telecommunications Plc agreed to merge in a deal valued at more than $20 billion. Rumors that the companies were in talks emerged Friday afternoon but the deal was formally announced Sunday. BT has a 20 percent stake already in MCI.
MCI hit 33-3/8, up 3-1/8 in U.S. pre-open trading on Monday. BT ADRs surged 6-3/8 to 61-7/8.

Norfolk Southern Corp said it is in talks with CSX Corp about their respective offers to buy Conrail Inc. Conrail lost 8-1/4 to 87 in U.S. pre-open trading amid disappointment that a bidding war appeared less likely.

Southern National Corp and United Carolina Bancshares said their boards approved a stock-swap merger valued at $985 million. UCB shareholders will receive 1.135 shares of Southern National for each UCB share. The deal will be accounted for as a pooling of interests.

Britain's Invesco Plc said it planned to merge with AIM Management Group Inc, one of the largest and fastest-growing mutual fund managers in the United States, to create a group with funds under management in excess of 90 billion pounds ($147 billion). Under the pact, Invesco will take a majority holding in an enlarged group to be renamed AMVESCO Plc. Invesco said AIM was being valued at about $1.6 billion.
Sierra Health Services Inc said it definitively agreed to merge with Physician Corp of America.

The deal would create the eighth-largest publicly traded U.S. managed care company with $2 billion in revenue. The deal would be accounted for as a tax-free pooling of interests, with each Physician Corp of America share being exchanged for 0.45 share of Sierra Health Services.

On Sunday, J.C. Penney Co Inc and Eckerd Corp said Penney will acquire Eckerd for cash and stock in a deal valued at about $3.3 billion. The acquisition, which has been approved by both boards, will be completed in two steps.

Penney said the first step calls for it to offer $35 per share cash for about 37.1 million shares, or 50.1 percent, of Eckerd. The balance of the purchase will be made through a stock swap, in which Eckerd shareholders will receive 0.6604 of a Penney share for each Eckerd share.
